For the project threshold, Hays County is supported by the Purola Preserve flora and recent Hays County field documentation; Travis County is supported by the UT Plant Resources Center herbarium index; Bandera County is independently supported by a documented Lost Maples photograph. tags: Corona Hoods (hornless or without projecting horns)

morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous perennial from stout rootstocks; stems usually clustered, ascending to somewhat decumbent, about 20–60 cm tall.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Alternate to subopposite, sometimes irregularly crowded; leaf arrangement overlaps with green milkweed.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, about 1–3 cm wide, usually narrowly acuminate; often visibly narrower than A. viridis.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Terminal, usually solitary, many-flowered and very crowded; peduncle length varies.
morphology_keys.flower_color: Pale yellowish-green, sometimes purple-flushed; corona may show darker purple hoods.
morphology_keys.gynostegium_detail: Five corona hoods are present. UT's detailed account of A. asperula subsp. capricornu describes each hood as lacking an enclosed horn. Do not teach 'A. asperula horned versus A. viridis hornless' as the species split; a hood is not the same thing as a horn. Subspecific hood color and form vary.
morphology_keys.fruit: Paired or solitary follicles; mature pods split to release comose seeds.
morphology_keys.joey_field_note: In Edwards Plateau Botany Part II, Joey shows a clear flowering umbel and uses the flower cluster to reinforce milkweed corona/hood structure.

fastest_traits: Five corona hoods; no dependable projecting-horn distinction from A. viridis
field_diagnostics.separation_from_viridis: TPWD emphasizes leaf shape: A. asperula tends toward narrow lanceolate to linear-lanceolate leaves with narrowly acuminate/attenuate tips, while A. viridis tends toward broader oblong to ovate leaves with rounded/obtuse to shortly acute tips. FNA additionally separates the species by relative corona segment length: A. viridis segments < half the corolla-lobe length. A. asperula often inhabits rocky uplands and has more globose crowded umbels; all traits can overlap, and hybrids are known outside the Central Texas focal zone.

ecological_notes.habitat: Rocky and sandy prairies of the Blackland Prairie, Edwards Plateau, Grand Prairie, Rolling Plains, High Plains and Trans-Pecos.
ecological_notes.central_texas_note: Well documented in Hays County and elsewhere across the Edwards Plateau / Central Texas.
ecological_notes.host_status: An important native monarch larval host in Texas; also supports other milkweed-associated insects and pollinators.

look_here_first: Inspect mature leaf shape and tip: antelopehorns usually has much narrower lanceolate/linear-lanceolate leaves, narrowly tapering to an acute point. Check dense terminal flower heads, often more rounded than in A. viridis, but do not use head shape alone. Its five corona hoods are present; a projecting horn is not the reliable split from A. viridis.
